card.name: Čoček
card.era: Arose early 19th century from Ottoman military bands; modern Romani form across 19th-20th c.
card.tagline: Ottoman-rooted Romani brass-band dance of the Balkans - line and solo.
card.profile: Čoček is a musical genre and dance that emerged in the Balkans in the early 19th century and features prominently in the repertoire of Romani brass bands (Wikipedia). It originated from Ottoman military bands scattered across Serbia, Bulgaria, North Macedonia and Romania, preserved mostly by Roma communities and performed at weddings and banquets. It exists in two forms: a communal line/circle dance (in Macedonia often called 'oro'), and an improvised solo women's dance using hand gestures, pelvic and abdominal isolations and shoulder shakes (Carol Silverman, Romani Routes, 2012). The music is played by brass bands, clarinet, zurna and tapan in syncopated 2/4, 7/8 and 9/8 meters.
card.insight: Čoček is central to Romani identity and Balkan brass-band culture; ethnomusicologist Carol Silverman calls it the most characteristic Romani solo dance (Romani Routes, Oxford University Press, 2012). It anchors Serbia's Guča Trumpet Festival and the film music of Goran Bregović.
